title: Iran-Contra Affair: Shady in the 80s, Part 1
summary: Part one of a two-part Stuff You Should Know episode on the Iran-Contra affair. The hosts cover Reagan's anti-communism and the Reagan Doctrine, US involvement in Nicaragua going back to the Banana Wars, the Contras and the Sandinista government, and Congress's Boland Amendments after Newsweek and Wall Street Journal reporting. They describe the CIA harbor mining in Nicaragua, Oliver North's role, the private fundraising nonprofit, the Richard Secord and Albert Hakim "Enterprise" arms network, and the domestic propaganda office and sting operations. The episode ends with a teaser for part two and a promotional call to action.
topics: National Endowment for the Preservation of Liberty

segments.title: Tour dates and opening banter
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck plug upcoming tour dates, then chat about Stranger Things and their 1980s-themed outfits and the upcoming Iran-Contra topic.

segments.title: Reagan, communism, and the Reagan Doctrine
segments.summary: The hosts describe Reagan's anti-communism from his Hollywood years and his presidency, and the Reagan Doctrine of aiding anti-communist forces.

segments.title: Nicaragua, the Sandinistas, and US history there
segments.summary: The Sandinistas took power in Nicaragua; the hosts trace US occupation from 1912 to 1933 during the Banana Wars, and Reagan's focus on the Sandinista government and its Soviet and Cuban ties.

segments.title: Contras funding and Congress turns against it
segments.summary: The US funds and trains the right-wing Contra rebels in secret. The Democrats take the House in the midterms, and a Newsweek cover story prompts Representative Edward Boland to challenge the policy. Dewey Clarridge's poor briefings to Congress are discussed.

segments.title: Harbor mining and the Boland Amendments
segments.summary: The Boland Amendment bars CIA and Defense funds for the Contras. The CIA mines Nicaraguan harbors, damaging ships from several countries; the Wall Street Journal reports it, and Congress passes further amendments closing loopholes.

segments.title: Mid-episode break
segments.summary: Short break before the next segment.

segments.title: Covert workaround and Oliver North's role
segments.summary: Reagan keeps operations underground and runs a public campaign against Congress. The National Security Council takes over with Robert McFarlane and John Poindexter, and Lieutenant Colonel Oliver North runs the operation.

segments.title: Private fundraising, the Enterprise, and arms dealers
segments.summary: North raises private funds through a nonprofit, the National Endowment for the Preservation of Liberty, which raised about six million dollars with Saudi Arabia donating heavily. Richard Secord and Albert Hakim build the Enterprise, a shell network of arms dealers and Swiss accounts, and Edwin Wilson's illegal arms trading is described.
topics: National Endowment for the Preservation of Liberty

segments.title: Secord takes over Contra arms supply
segments.summary: Secord and Hakim's operation grows; North places the Contra leaders under Secord, who handles arms and airdrops, with the enterprise investing in planes and airstrips.

segments.title: Break
segments.summary: Short break before the propaganda segment.

segments.title: Propaganda campaign, Office of Public Diplomacy, and sting operations
segments.summary: The Office of Public Diplomacy, run by Otto Reich, runs a propaganda campaign despite Reagan's executive order banning CIA domestic influence. Sting operations include a staged cocaine photo of a Sandinista official and a failed plot involving Manuel Noriega. Journalists were allegedly pressured and smeared.

segments.title: Teaser and sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts tease part two and ask listeners to share the show and leave reviews.
